summary: Ankur Barua works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong under Dorothy C. Wong, and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. in anthropology from the University of Chicago (~1971–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1984–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Charles Willemen (~1989–1998). She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who studied at Barnard College (B.A.) and Columbia University (M.A.). She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and the University of Michigan (1989–2004), and served as founding director at The New School (2004).
Anna A. Golovkova is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at Lake Forest College and Cornell University (attested 2020).
Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Indologist Anna Aurelia Esposito studied at the University of Tübingen (MA, 1998), Heidelberg University, and the University of Würzburg. She served as Assistant Professor at Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and held a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning a PhD at SOAS under Lionel Caplan, Lopen Dugyal, and Gorlok Tulku. She held posts at the Bulletin of Tibetology and Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (2002).
Anna Brown is a scholar in religious studies and other fields who studied Zen under Robert Kennedy. She served as department chair and program director at Saint Peter's University (attested 2017).

Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She held posts with the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan, University of Naples "L'Orientale," and University of Naples Federico II.

Anna Halafoff is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Melbourne, the University of New England, and Monash University, and held a post at Deakin University.

Anna Kamensky was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at Bestuzhev Courses and the University of Geneva (~1922–1926), later serving at the University of Geneva as PD in comparative religion (~1928–1950).

Anna Kramskova specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (2014–2016) and held a research assistant post at the Institute of Linguistic Studies, Russian Academy of Sciences (2019).
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist. She held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and became a Professor at Princeton University in 2015.
Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi, and completed a PhD at Heidelberg University.
Anna Scarabel is an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at Heidelberg University in 2018. She later joined the faculty at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied in Munich, Hamburg, and Paris under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. Her career included posts at EFEO, Institut du Hōbōgirin, Hawaiʻi, and UC Santa Barbara.

Anna Stirr is an Indologist educated at Lawrence University and Columbia University (PhD 2009). She held posts at The New School (2009), University of Oxford (2009–2011), Leiden University (2011), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2012).
